From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Scaling pathway with voucher offsets and co-term options

Hi Aurelia —

Great talking with you earlier. Per our conversation, here is a simple path to scale CloudMira's capacity mid-contract while keeping the renewal co-term aligned in April:

Summary proposal (high level)
- Immediate uplift: +30% committed capacity starting today (effective 2026-11-10)
- Voucher offset: $45,000 one-time credit applied across the next 3 invoices to smooth the cost impact
- Co-term: align new capacity to co-term on 2027-04-01; remaining pro-rata for this partial period will be invoiced monthly

Why this helps:
- Keeps procurement comfortable with incremental spend rather than a single big invoice
- Preserves your target renewal cadence (April) so you only reprice once at renewal
- Voucher offsets make bookkeeping straightforward for Finance (credit line item)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm you and Procurement are comfortable with the $45k voucher offset approach
2) If yes, Ben and I will draft an amendment (short form) and route for signature; Rachel from Finance will sign off on invoice timing
3) We can also push a draft DocuSign today if you want an executed amendment before the uplift goes live

Attached: CloudMira_Uplift_Summary_20261110.pdf — includes expected monthly invoices with credit applied.

Open questions I want to flag:
- Do you need the voucher split across more than 3 invoices?
- Will Procurement require a PO number before we process the uplift?

Thanks, Aurelia — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — really appreciate the quick summary. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit: 

1) Voucher split: can the $45k be spread across 6 invoices instead of 3? That would keep our monthly budget smoother.
2) PO requirement: yes, procurement requires a PO for any amendment > $10k. They can issue a PO quickly once we have the amendment language and total invoice schedule.
3) Legal/terms: we need to confirm there are no new data residency or SLA changes in the amendment; if it's strictly capacity and pricing, legal is OK with a short-form amendment.

Also looping in Jamal from Engineering — he wanted to confirm that the +30% is sufficient for the next quarter; Jamal, if you see any spikes that would push us past that, flag it and we'll talk throughput-based burst options.

If you can send a short amendment draft with the 6-invoice voucher split, we can circulate it to Procurement and Legal.

Best,

Agreed path (final)
- Effective uplift: 2026-11-10 (30% capacity increase)
- Voucher total: $45,000 split across 6 monthly invoices (7,500 credit applied per invoice) starting with the current invoice cycle (Nov 2026)
- Pro-rata billing: partial period 2026-11-10 to 2027-04-01 invoiced monthly for the uplift portion; April 1, 2027 onward billed against the new co-term annual commitment
- Total incremental spend (net of credits) through 2027-04-01: $120,000 (this is the gross uplift less voucher application; detailed breakdown in attached amendment)

1) Procurement: please issue a PO referencing amendment ID AMND-2026-11-CM (we'll include that in the DocuSign envelope). PO should reference the attached amendment and the invoice schedule.
2) CloudMira Legal: if you have no further redlines, we'll push the DocuSign for signature today.
